Column normalization ON TOP of row normalization. Row norm makes each neuron's gradient unit-length; col norm makes each feature's gradient unit-length. Dual-axis normalization.
Column norm INSTEAD of row norm. Tests whether per-feature normalization is better than per-neuron for polar express input.
Blend 5% sign(gradient) into orthogonalized update. Sign gradient has zero mean — acts as implicit regularization. Small mix to avoid instability.
10% sign gradient blending. Stronger regularization signal.
Skip orthogonalization 10% of steps. Injects raw gradient signal as regularization — prevents Muon from over-constraining update directions.
Skip orthogonalization 20% of steps. Stronger raw gradient injection.
Blend 30% raw normalized gradient with 70% orthogonalized. Soft orthogonalization — less aggressive than full polar express.
50/50 blend of raw and orthogonalized gradient. Tests whether full ortho is too aggressive.
Sine-gated linear unit: sin(Wx) * Vx. Periodic activation creates oscillating gate — radically different from monotonic gates like SiLU/ELU.
Tanh-gated linear unit: tanh(Wx) * Vx. Bounded smooth gate in [-1,1] — allows negative gating unlike sigmoid-based GLUs.
Laplace-gated linear unit: laplace_cdf(Wx) * Vx. Exponential-decay gating — sharper transitions than sigmoid.
Triple-projection GLU: three learned projections instead of two. More parameters per layer but richer gating dynamics.
Cosine similarity attention: L2-normalize Q and K. Tested before on weaker baselines (neutral/loser) — row+rms Muon may change the dynamics.
HiLo attention: split heads into 25% high-frequency (local window) and 75% low-frequency (global). Multi-scale attention at no extra cost.
HiLo attention: 50/50 split between local and global heads.

Cosine gate is periodic like singlu's sin — tests whether cos periodicity works in bilinear form.
Mish (x*tanh(softplus(x))) is smooth non-monotonic — similar flavor to sin's periodicity.
Gaussian gate exp(-x²) creates bell-shaped activation — soft local attention in FFN space.
Squared gate (x²) creates magnitude-only activation — sign-agnostic gating.
Cubic gate (x³) preserves sign with polynomial amplification — sharper than linear.
Squared SiLU gate — tests sharper version of SiLU that amplifies confident activations.
Absolute value gate |x| — simplest magnitude-only gate, tests pure magnitude hypothesis.

Triple-projection: SiLU(g)×up×sigmoid(aux) — 3-way multiplicative interaction for richer gating.
LeakyReLU gate × linear — negative slope preserves gradient flow unlike ReLU, but still piecewise linear.

ReGLU (ReLU gate × linear) — simplest piecewise-linear gate, strong baseline in some settings.
